assertion.statement: The conductor of the modular realization of the same final f equals v_p(N), including bad and dyadic primes.
assertion.objects: For the D6 beta family only: The modular realization of the final primitive normalized weight-two form f of level N.
assertion.hypotheses: f has its actual arbitrary coefficient field and nebentypus, with the same selected coefficient embedding as the comparison.
assertion.quantifiers: Every rational residue prime p and every coefficient prime ell different from p.
assertion.parameter_range: All bad primes and dyadic primes are included; no squarefree-level or rational-coefficient hypothesis.
assertion.uniformity: The theorem is applied to the same final form at each allowed auxiliary coefficient prime.
assertion.constants: a_p(U_f,ell)=v_p(N). No numerical upper bound on N is supplied by this theorem.
assertion.normalizations: The Tate/cohomological dual and the unramified norm convention preserve the full Artin or Weil-Deligne conductor.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The theorem does not apply at p=ell. A different auxiliary ell handles each p; no extraordinary-cuspidal exclusion remains in the final theorem.
assertion.limit_order: Use Carayol section2.4 with the final Theorem4 and its stated consequence; transfer to the geometric family only through the separate actual local isomorphism.

use.reason: Apply the direct published conductor theorem at ell different from p. Combine its modular-side equality with the separate actual-family local isomorphism. Do not invoke the historical Casselman intermediary or use r_5 at residue characteristic5.

supplier.statement: For a primitive normalized weight-two form f, the full conductor exponent of its modular realization at p is v_p(N_f), for ell different from p.
